name: Not A Sheep
description: A very small horse that is, by every appearance, a sheep. Mostly creamy white, sometimes black, moorit brown, roan-grey or pied, now and then pale-bellied like a wild mouflon. The rams are usually horned - curled, mostly, though some carry four horns and a few just scurs - and the ewes usually are not. It is not a sheep. Please stop trying to shear it.
notes: Owner's spec, 2026-10-01: sheep-sized (a small pony, Shetland-sized), every natural sheep colour as solids, plus the sheep patterns that have a close natural gene already in the mod, horned like real flocks, and in all ways resembling a sheep.

WHITE, MOSTLY. Real flocks are mostly white, and the closest natural horse is double cream: Cr/Cr over chestnut is a cremello, over black a smoky cream, both near-white. Cream 70 x any extension makes about seven in ten white.

THE OTHER SOLIDS. Moorit brown is a chestnut (e/e, no cream) - about one in five. Black is E/E a/a with no cream - under one in twelve. Grey sheep are a dark fleece with white fibres through it, which is roan (Rn/rn, one in twelve) - blue roan on black, red roan on moorit, and lost on a white one, as a grey fleece would be.

THE PATTERNS WITH A NATURAL GENE. Pied sheep (Jacob) are tobiano, one in ten. Mouflon - a darker body with a pale belly and muzzle - is pangare, shown best on the rare bay (E/E A/A); on a moorit it is the pale-bellied brown. Patterns with no close natural gene - the Suffolk's black face and legs on a white body, badger-face - are left out, per the spec.

HORNS LIKE REAL FLOCKS. Mostly the rams-only allele: about seven in ten rams and fifteen in a hundred ewes are horned, the rest polled. Curled in about four in five; four-horned (Jacob) about one in eight, scurs one in twenty, corkscrew rare. Horns pale to dark (shade 0 to 0.75), no coloured tips.
No wool, no bleating: wool does not exist yet in the mod (its own design session), and the owner chose horns as the sheep feature for now.
